concepts.title: Types of Networks LAN MAN WAN
concepts.definition: Networks are classified by the area they span: a LAN connects computers within a building or campus, a MAN spans a city such as cable networks across town, and a WAN spans countries or the world, with the Internet as the largest WAN. Smaller reach generally means faster speeds and cheaper ownership.
concepts.key_idea: A LAN is privately owned and measured in metres to kilometres; a WAN uses leased public carrier links across cities and nations. PAN (personal area, e.g. Bluetooth headset) is smaller still.
question_patterns: Which network type connects computers within one school building?

worked_examples.q: Which network type spans a building or campus?

concepts.title: Network Devices Repeater Switch Router
concepts.definition: Network devices connect and direct traffic: a repeater regenerates a weakening signal, a hub broadcasts incoming data to every port, a switch forwards frames only to the intended port using MAC addresses, a router connects different networks and routes packets between them, a modem modulates digital data onto carrier lines, and a gateway translates between different protocol systems.
concepts.key_idea: The intelligence rises up the chain: repeater amplifies, hub shouts to everyone, switch selects the port, router selects the network, gateway translates protocols. A switch learns MAC addresses; a hub never does.
question_patterns: Which device regenerates a weakening signal to extend cable length?

worked_examples.q: Which device regenerates a weakening signal?

concepts.title: Bandwidth and Data Transfer Time
concepts.definition: Bandwidth is the data-carrying capacity of a channel, measured in bits per second. Transfer time follows from the size of the file in bits divided by the bandwidth: a file of f megabytes over a link of b megabits per second takes f x 8 / b seconds, since one byte is eight bits.
concepts.key_idea: Always convert the file size to bits before dividing by the bit rate. The 8x byte-to-bit factor is the step students most often miss; prefixes matter too (1 Mbps is one million bits per second in networking).
question_patterns: How long does it take to transfer a {mb} MB file over a {mbps} Mbps link?

worked_examples.q: How many bits are in one byte -- the factor most often missed in transfer-time sums?

concepts.title: Web Address URL and DNS
concepts.definition: A URL locates a resource: protocol, domain and path, such as https://www.example.com/index.html. The Domain Name System (DNS) translates the human-readable domain into the numeric IP address that machines route by, like a phonebook for the Internet.
concepts.key_idea: Computers route by IP address, humans remember names; DNS resolves the name to the address before the request leaves. https differs from http by the TLS encryption layer.

concepts.title: Network Topologies Star Bus Tree
concepts.definition: Topology is the layout that connects nodes. In a bus every node taps one shared backbone; in a star every node links to a central switch; a tree joins multiple stars onto a backbone. Star failure of the central device downs the whole network, while in a bus a broken backbone splits it.
concepts.key_idea: Cabling cost and fault tolerance trade off: star needs the most cable but isolates link failures to one node; bus is cheapest but one cable fault affects many. Mesh, with every node linked to every other, is the most fault-tolerant and the most expensive.
question_patterns: Which topology connects every node to a central switch?

worked_examples.q: Which topology taps one shared backbone wire?

concepts.title: Voice over Internet Protocol and Video Conferencing
concepts.definition: Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) carries telephone calls as packets over IP networks instead of dedicated phone lines, and video conferencing joins distant sites with live two-way audio and video. Both need steady bandwidth and low delay to stay usable.
concepts.key_idea: Applications are classed by tolerance: file transfer tolerates delay, live voice and video do not, which is why conferencing quality tracks available bandwidth and latency.
question_patterns: What is VoIP and how does it differ from traditional telephony?
Name two applications that need low network delay.
Which technology lets two schools hold a live two-way class?
Why does a video call degrade when bandwidth drops?
Give one advantage and one limitation of VoIP.

worked_examples.q: What does VoIP carry as packets over IP networks?
How long does a 40 MB file take to transfer over a 20 Mbps link?
worked_examples.a: Convert to bits: 40 x 8 = 320 megabits. Divide by the rate: 320 / 20 = 16 seconds. Ignoring protocol overheads, the transfer takes about 16 seconds.

worked_examples.q: A school lab has 30 computers on a star topology. One computer's cable is damaged. Who is affected?
worked_examples.a: Only that one computer loses its link - in a star topology each node has its own cable to the central switch, so a single cable fault isolates a single node. Only failure of the central switch itself would take down the whole lab.
